feedback: FINAL_STATES header is present and u3 is declared, but the machine fails the task's ordering requirement. Task: 'Take the key only after the ball is out of the way, then open the door and pick up the box.' The key must be acquired AFTER blocker_moved; however the transition (u0, blocker_moved & has_door_key) -> u1 rewards a step in which both hold simultaneously, meaning the key could be taken before the ball is moved (agent picks up key while ball still blocks: blocker_moved false, has_door_key true — that's fine in u0, but then u0's else self-loop keeps it there; actually the real problem is the opposite: the RM never requires has_door_key at all). The transitions (u0, blocker_moved) -> u1 and (u1, door_open) -> u2 allow reaching u3 with door_open granted without ever holding the key — door_open cannot occur without the key, so those branches are harmless in that respect, but they also skip verification that the key was taken after the ball move. Concretely: if the agent picks up the key (has_door_key true, blocker_moved false, stays in u0), drops it (key_lost fires, ignored), picks up the ball (blocker_moved -> u1, reward 0.1, no credit for key), then must re-take the key — acceptable — but the dual-transitions with weaker predicates (door_open alone, blocker_moved alone) are redundant since door_open implies has_door_key and blocker_moved & has_door_key implies blocker_moved; they add unreachable/ambiguous branches. Also key_lost is never used: the task says take the key after the ball is moved; if the agent takes the key first (allowed by env), the RM cannot detect or penalize this regression, since key_lost and re-acquisition of has_door_key are not distinguished from first acquisition. The machine cannot distinguish 'key taken after ball move' from 'key re-taken after being lost' — but more importantly it never requires the key-holding state before door_open at all, so the 'take the key' stage is not enforced. Compactness: duplicate transitions ((u0, blocker_moved & has_door_key) and (u0, blocker_moved) both to u1; same for u1) — the stronger predicate subsumes the weaker, so the pair is redundant and rewards are ambiguous (a single step satisfies both patterns; ordering/precedence of reward application is undefined). No FINAL_STATES acceptance semantics issue beyond u3, else self-loops correctly cover irrelevant events. Fix by restructuring: u0 --(blocker_moved)--> u1 --(has_door_key)--> u2 --(door_open)--> u3 --(target_picked_up)--> u4, dropping redundant weaker transitions, with dense bounded progress rewards and explicit handling of key_lost regression if re-acquisition after loss must be penalized or tolerated per task intent.

feedback: The RM correctly encodes the required order: blocker_moved before key acquisition (u0->u1 on blocker_moved, only then has_door_key to u2), then door_open to u3, then target_picked_up to u4. Nonempty FINAL_STATES header present with u4 declared and accepting; all states declared. All five propositions appear in the transition function, and per-state else self-loops cover irrelevant events, including regressions: the u2 branch (!has_door_key & door_open) handles the key_lost-style drop where the key is released (has_door_key false) while the door opens in the same or later step sequence; blocker_moved regression (ball dropped back) leaves u1 unchanged, which is safe since the ordering constraint only requires the ball be moved before key pickup in this task's intended path — note blocker_moved turning false again in u1 does not regress the state, matching the explicit reading. Progress rewards are dense-in-event, bounded (0.15+0.15+0.2+0.5 = 1.0), and non-negative. Predicate-only events used throughout. No unsafe reward holes: key first then ball path fires key_lost (has_door_key drops while door closed) which is covered by the else loop in u2 without spurious rewards. Minor note: the task says 'Take the key only after the ball is out of the way,' which u1 enforces. No issues found.

blocker_moved is incorrect. The documented reading is 'the cell in front of the door holds no ball' (env.grid.get(dx-1, dy) has no ball); the candidate instead requires that NO cell anywhere holds a ball (ignoring the ball-in-hand case is wrong too: with the ball carried, grid has no ball so candidate is true regardless of the ball's dropped position — actually candidate semantics: no ball on grid AND a door exists AND no door has a ball at (xx-1,yy). Checking a random (xx-1,yy) cell for every door is not 'the cell in front of the door' and the expression's structure is convoluted/incorrect: it scans all (xx,yy) pairs and tests grid.get(xx-1, yy) for each, which only happens to match when the ball was dropped at an arbitrary cell, deviating from the spec (ball dropped anywhere but in front of door should keep blocker_moved true). Rewrite blocker_moved to locate the single door and test env.grid.get(door_x - 1, door_y) for a ball, per the code notes.

The key_lost predicate correctly implements the event semantics and all other functions match the documented expressions, but blocker_moved deviates from the specified truth condition. Its expression 'any(cell is not None and cell.type == "door" and env.grid.get(x - 1, y) is not None and env.grid.get(x - 1, y).type == "ball" ...) == False' negates the whole check, which yields True whenever there is no door whose left neighbor is a ball. However, the specification says blocker_moved is true when 'the cell in front of the door holds no ball'. The candidate checks the cell at (x-1, y) relative to every scanned cell, not specifically the cell in front of the door on the start side, and it negates the entire grid scan rather than checking the absence of a ball at the door's front cell. For example, in a grid where the door exists and no ball is anywhere, the candidate returns True for blocker_moved, which could be correct, but the negation flips semantics: it returns False when a ball is at (dx-1, dy) only if there is also a door there, conflating two different conditions. This means blocker_moved may incorrectly report False (or True) in states where the specification requires the opposite, since the negation applies to whether any door has a ball to its left rather than whether the specific blocking cell is free of a ball. This breaks the RM transition (u0, blocker_moved) -> u1 and can fire early or late relative to the true condition. Fix blocker_moved to directly check that the cell in front of the door holds no ball, matching the documented expression: not any(cell is not None and cell.type == 'ball' for cell in [env.grid.get(dx - 1, dy)]) with the door located by type scan.
